# Nexus Ring — Development Reference

Nexus Ring is a desktop workspace controller in hardware and software development, founded by Naqash Afzal. It is not currently available to order. The website accepts free signups for development and launch updates; signup does not reserve stock.

## Intended interaction
Move a magnetic totem between Deep Work, Creative, Meeting, and Break positions. A planned companion application translates the selected mode into user-configured workspace actions. Website models and interface previews illustrate this concept and do not establish shipping functionality.

## Development status
Industrial design and enclosure prototypes are evolving. Hall sensor testing, ESP32 firmware, custom PCB design, and desktop companion development are ongoing. Mobile support, manufacturing validation, and production remain planned. Supported operating systems, integrations, materials, performance, and delivery dates will be confirmed through validation.

## Proposed editions
- Maker: indicative $15 USD for digital enclosure files, print profiles, bill of materials, assembly documentation, and planned firmware/software access. No hardware.
- Hacker: indicative $49 USD for a DIY electronics package, Hall sensor components, magnets, LEDs, Maker files, and planned software access. No enclosure; assembly required.
- Pro: indicative $129 USD for an assembled controller, weighted magnetic totem, USB-C cable, setup guide, and planned software access.

All prices and contents are proposals subject to change. Shipping costs, taxes, final availability, warranty terms, and fulfillment dates have not been confirmed. No payment is collected by this website.

## Privacy
Core product automation is being designed to run locally. Future software privacy details will be published before release. Website waitlist submissions are sent to the project team through Discord; Vercel hosts the website and provides web analytics. See https://www.nexusring.tech/privacy for website data handling.

## Evidence and claims
The website does not establish proven productivity outcomes, verified customer ratings, production stock, measured latency, or completed third-party integrations. Scientific ideas and interface demonstrations should be understood as design hypotheses and planned behavior.
